chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
There is no shortening (of prayer) upon the sailors in their ships, nor upon the hirers (of animals) and the cameleers.
And in another report: The hirer, when the journey extends for him, let him shorten (his prayer).
He said: And the meaning of 'the journey extends for him' is that he makes two stages (of travel) into one stage.

key_terms.الْجَمَّالِ: Cameleers or those who use camels for transport
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: Those who hire animals (e.g., for riding or transport)
key_terms.تَقْصِير: Shortening of the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs during travel
key_terms.جَدَّ بِهِ السَّيْرُ: The journey extended/continued for him (indicating a long duration)

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from shortening prayers while traveling according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between professional travel and leisure travel, establishing that sailors and camel drivers are exempt from shortening prayers (qasr) unless the journey becomes arduous ('jadda bihi al-sayr'). The text provides a practical metric for this exemption, defining an extended journey as one requiring two overnight stops, thereby linking the physical hardship of travel to the legal concession. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) in religious obligations for those engaged in continuous occupational travel.

en.hubeali:
Muhamad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala, form Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The shortening is not upon the sailors in their ships, nor upon the hirers (of animals) and the cameleers’.
And in another report: ‘The hirer (of animals), when the journey extends for him, so let him shorten’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And the meaning of ‘journey extends for him’, is that he makes the two destinations as one destination (i.e. halves the journey)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Sailors when in their vessel are not required to perform their Salah (prayer) as reduced as well as muleteers and camel drivers.’
In another Hadith it is said that muleteers perform their Salah (prayer) as reduced when the journey becomes condensed,
like walking two days of journey in one day.’”
